facts.statement: Centrosaurus fossils were found in the Dinosaur Park Formation in Canada and date to between 76.5 and 75.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its remains have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation, dating from 76.5 to 75.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Scientists speculate that large Centrosaurus bonebeds formed when herds died while trying to cross flooded rivers.
facts.quote: Scientists have speculated that the high density and number of individuals would be explained if they had perished while trying to cross a flooded river.

facts.statement: Centrosaurus reached lengths of 5 to 5.5 meters and masses of 2 to 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Centrosaurus were large dinosaurs, although not as large as some of their relatives, reaching 5 - 5.5 m long and 2 - 2.5 MT in body mass situated atop stocky limbs.

facts.statement: Centrosaurus is distinguished by two large hornlets that hook forward over the frill.
facts.quote: Centrosaurus is distinguished by having two large hornlets which hook forwards over the frill.

facts.statement: Centrosaurus had a pair of small horns directed upward over the eyes.
facts.quote: A pair of small upwards directed horns is also found over the eyes.

facts.statement: The Centrosaurus frill could grow to over 68.8 cm in length in the largest adults.
facts.quote: The frill was relatively short compared to the total skull length and could grow to over half a meter (68.8 cm) long in the oldest and largest adults.

facts.statement: The genus Centrosaurus gives its name to the Centrosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: The genus Centrosaurus gives its name to the Centrosaurinae subfamily.

facts.statement: The closest relatives of Centrosaurus appear to be Styracosaurus and Monoclonius.
facts.quote: Its closest relatives appear to be Styracosaurus and Monoclonius.

facts.statement: Gigantic bone beds suggest that Centrosaurus were gregarious animals that traveled in large herds.
facts.quote: The discovery of gigantic bone beds of Centrosaurus in Canada suggest that they were gregarious animals and could have traveled in large herds.

facts.statement: A 2009 study found that skull lesions in Centrosaurus were likely caused by intraspecific combat rather than predatory attacks.
facts.quote: A 2009 study of Triceratops and Centrosaurus skull lesions found that bone injuries on the skulls were more likely caused by intraspecific combat (horn-to-horn combat) rather than predatory attacks.

facts.statement: The frills of Centrosaurus were too thin to defend against predators, unlike the thicker frills of Triceratops.
facts.quote: The frills of Centrosaurus were too thin to be used for defense against predators, although the thicker, solid frills of Triceratops might have evolved to protect their necks.

facts.statement: A Centrosaurus specimen found in 1989 had crippling osteosarcoma in its right fibula.
facts.quote: A specimen of Centrosaurus apertus recovered from Dinosaur Provincial Park in 1989 was discovered to have crippling osteosarcoma in its right fibula.

facts.statement: Being part of a herd allowed the Centrosaurus with severe cancer to survive longer than expected.
facts.quote: However, the fact that it was part of a herd allowed the Centrosaurus to survive much longer than would be expected for an animal infected with such severe disease.

facts.statement: There is debate over whether Centrosaurus and Monoclonius are valid genera or represent members of the opposite sex.
facts.quote: Because of the variation between species and even individual specimens of centrosaurines, there has been much debate over which genera and species are valid, particularly whether Centrosaurus and/or Monoclonius are valid genera, undiagnosable, or possibly members of the opposite sex.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson argued in 1996 that Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Monoclonius warrant separate genera.
facts.quote: In 1996, Peter Dodson found enough variation between Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Monoclonius to warrant separate genera and that Styracosaurus resembled Centrosaurus more closely than either resembled Monoclonius.

facts.statement: While sexual dimorphism is proposed for Protoceratops, there is no firm evidence for it in any ceratopsid.
facts.quote: While sexual dimorphism has been proposed for a more basal ceratopsian, Protoceratops, there is no firm evidence for sexual dimorphism in any ceratopsid.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that C. nasicornus is the direct ancestor of Styracosaurus albertensis.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested as the direct ancestor of Styracosaurus albertensis.

facts.statement: Centrosaurus fossils have only been found in southern Alberta despite the region's abundance of Judithian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Thomas M. Lehman has observed that Centrosaurus fossils haven't been found outside of southern Alberta even though they are among the most abundant Judithian dinosaurs in the region.

facts.statement: Centrosaurus had a massive body supported by robust legs and measured about 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Los cuerpos masivos de Centrosaurus fueron soportados por extremidades robustas, media unos 6 metros de largo

facts.statement: Centrosaurus possessed a single nose horn that could curve forward or backward depending on the individual.
facts.quote: presentaban un solo cuerno sobre la nariz como otro centrosaurinos, el cual podía curvarse hacia adelante o hacia atrás, dependiendo del individuo

facts.statement: The frill of Centrosaurus was moderately long with fairly large windows and small horns along the outer edge.
facts.quote: El volante de Centrosaurus era moderadamente largo, con ventanas bastante grandes y pequeños cuernos a lo largo del borde externo

facts.statement: C. apertus is distinguished by having two large hook-like horns at the tip of the frill.
facts.quote: C. apertus se distingue por tener dos cuernos grandes como ganchos sobre el extremo del volante

facts.statement: A pair of small horns located above the eyes in Centrosaurus apertus point upward.
facts.quote: Un par de pequeños cuernos también se encuentra sobre los ojos, en Centrosaurus apertus éstos se dirigen hacia arriba

facts.statement: Like other ceratopsids, Centrosaurus jaws were adapted to shear through tough plant material.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros ceratópsidos, las mandíbulas de los centrosaurios estaban adaptadas para cortar material vegetal resistente

facts.statement: The first Centrosaurus fossil was discovered by Lawrence Lambe in Alberta, Canada, along the Red Deer River.
facts.quote: El primer fósil Centrosaurus fue descubierto por Lawrence Lambe en la provincia canadiense de Alberta, a lo largo del Río Red Deer

facts.statement: Thousands of Centrosaurus fossils were found near Hilda, Alberta, believed to be the largest dinosaur bonebed ever discovered.
facts.quote: Se ha realizado un descubrimiento de miles de fósiles de Centrosaurus cerca de la ciudad de Hilda, Alberta, que se cree que es el lecho más grande de huesos de dinosaurios jamás descubierto

facts.statement: Massive Centrosaurus bonebeds in Alberta are thought to extend for kilometers and contain thousands of specimens of all ages and body conditions.
facts.quote: Se cree que estos yacimientos se extienden por kilómetros, contienendo miles de especímenes de todas las edades y constitución física

facts.statement: Scientists speculate that high densities of Centrosaurus fossils may result from individuals dying while attempting to cross a river during a flood.
facts.quote: Los científicos han especulado que la alta densidad y el número de individuos serían explicados si habían muerto mientras que intentaban cruzar un río durante una crecida

facts.statement: The name Centrosaurus derives from the Greek words for 'point' and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre proviene de griego κεντρον, kentron, "punta" con σαυρος, sauros, "lagarto"

facts.statement: The name refers to the series of small horns along the frill margin, not the nose horn, which was unknown when the dinosaur was named.
facts.quote: El nombre refiere a la serie de pequeños cuernos colocados a lo largo del margen del volante, y no al cuerno en su nariz, que era desconocido cuando el dinosaurio fue nombrado

facts.statement: Centrosaurus gives its name to the subfamily Centrosaurinae to which it belongs.
facts.quote: Centrosaurus le da el nombre a la subfamilia Centrosaurinae a la que pertenece

facts.statement: Centrosaurus has close relatives including Styracosaurus and Monoclonius.
facts.quote: Tiene como relativo cercanos a Styracosaurus y Monoclonius

facts.statement: There has been significant debate over whether Centrosaurus and Monoclonius are valid genera or possibly represent different sexes of the same species.
facts.quote: ha habido mucho debate sobre qué géneros y especies son válidos, particularmente si Centrosaurus y Monoclonius son géneros válidos, o no diagnosticables o posiblemente miembros de sexo opuesto

facts.statement: While sexual dimorphism has been proposed for the basal ceratopsian Protoceratops, there is no firm evidence of sexual dimorphism in any ceratopsian.
facts.quote: Mientras que el dimorfismo sexual se ha propuesto para un ceratopsiano más basal, Protoceratops, no hay evidencia firme de dimorfismo sexual en ningún ceratópsido

facts.statement: A 2014 study concluded that C. nasicornus is a junior synonym of C. apertus, representing a middle growth stage.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2014 de los cambios durante el crecimiento en Centrosaurus concluyó que C. nasicornus es un sinónimo más moderno de C. apertus , que representa una etapa de crecimiento medio

facts.statement: Large Centrosaurus bonebeds in Canada suggest they were gregarious animals that may have traveled in large herds.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento grandes lechos de huesos de Centrosaurus en Canadá sugiere que eran animales gregarios y que podrían haber viajado en grandes manadas

facts.statement: A 2009 study found that skull injuries in Centrosaurus were likely caused by intraspecific horn-to-horn combat rather than predator attacks.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2009 de las lesiones del cráneo de Triceratops y Centrosaurus encontró que las lesiones óseas en los cráneos eran más probablemente causadas por el combate intraespecífico, combate de cuerno a cuerno, en lugar de los ataques predatorios

facts.statement: Centrosaurus frills were too thin to be used as defense against predators.
facts.quote: Los collares de Centrosaurus eran demasiado delgados para ser utilizados como defensa contra los depredadores

facts.statement: Centrosaurus frills were likely used for species recognition or other forms of visual display.
facts.quote: Los collares de Centrosaurus probablemente se utilizaron "para el reconocimiento de especies u otras formas de visualización"

facts.statement: Fossils of Centrosaurus have not been found outside southern Alberta, despite being among the most abundant Judithian dinosaurs in the region.
facts.quote: Thomas M. Lehman ha observado que los fósiles de Centrosaurus no se han encontrado fuera del sur de Alberta a pesar de que se encuentran entre los dinosaurios del Juditiano más abundantes de la región

facts.statement: Large herbivorous ceratopsians in Late Cretaceous North America had notably small geographic ranges despite their large body size and high mobility.
facts.quote: Los grandes herbívoros como los ceratópsidos que vivían en Norteamérica durante el Cretácico superior tenían "rangos geográficos notablemente pequeños" a pesar de su gran tamaño corporal y alta movilidad

facts.statement: Centrosaurus occurs lower in the formation than Styracosaurus, indicating it was displaced by Styracosaurus as the environment changed over time.
facts.quote: Centrosaurus se encuentra más abajo en la formación que Styracosaurus, lo que indica que Centrosaurus fue desplazado por Styracosaurus ya que el entorno cambió con el tiempo

facts.statement: In 2020, an aggressive osteosarcoma cancer was described for the first time in a Centrosaurus apertus adult fossil from Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: En 2020 se describió por primera vez en un fósil de dinosaurio un osteosarcoma, un tipo de cáncer muy agresivo, en la fíbula de un Centrosaurus apertus adulto procedente del Parque provincial de los Dinosaurios (Alberta, Canadá)

facts.statement: Centrosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Centrosaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Centrosaurus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
